# Running wu025r005 in CESM

*Generated by Claude.*

How the [wu025r005 mesh](wave_mesh.md) is set up in CESM, what the first runs showed, and what is
still open. Status as of 2026-11-17.

## Registration and swapping meshes

`wu025r005` is registered in a development CESM sandbox, next to the small `wu2r05` test grid, in three
files: `components/ww3/cime_config/config_component.xml` (unstructured WW3 and the grid-input folder),
`namelist_definition_ww3.xml` (300 s timesteps, as for `wu025r004`), and
`ccs_config/component_grids_nuopc.xml` (the domain and its ESMF mesh). These edits are not upstream yet;
an upstream grid needs the final mesh staged in CESM inputdata under a dated name.

Every path points at one folder, `grid_inp/wu025r005`, which is a link to one staged build. To try a
new mesh, `mesh/tools/stage_grid.sh BUILD CASEROOT` (a ~10 min compute-node job) copies the build,
makes `mod_def.ww3` with the case's own `ww3_grid` (so it matches the case's WW3 build), writes the
ESMF mesh, and moves the link. The case then just resubmits: it sets `WW3_MODDEF` to the staged
`mod_def.ww3`, which `buildnml` copies whenever it changes. `WAV_NX`, `OCN_NX` and `ICE_NX` stay at
the first build's node count; the data models don't use them, and the mediator only uses them for
history dimensions.

## The smoke run

MESACLIP historical member 010 from 2000-01-01 for 2 days: DATM, DOCN and DICE in MESACLIP modes,
with DOCN and DICE on the wave mesh. WW3 ran both days, and `check_ww3_forcing.py` shows it received
the winds, currents, ice fraction and air-sea temperature the mediator sent (to about 1e-5). Ice
thickness stays at WW3's 0.5 m default, as in every earlier case.

Two setup lessons came out of it:

- **Give WW3 its own nodes.** With WW3 on 16 nodes and the data models and mediator on the first two
  of them (the layout used for `wu025r004`, which had no DOCN or DICE), the first run ran out of memory
  on node 2. WW3 needs about 1.4 GB per task at 2,048 tasks, mostly arrays every task keeps for the
  whole mesh. The case now puts WW3 on 16 nodes of its own (`ROOTPE_WAV=256`, 18 nodes in all).
- **Set `PIO_TYPENAME=pnetcdf`.** A case created with no matching `config_pes` entry starts with one
  task, and CIME then sets every component's I/O to serial `netcdf`; setting `NTASKS` later does not
  undo it. With serial I/O, WW3 took 48 minutes to write a 9.3 GB restart, and a 2-day test ran about
  11 times slower than the same run in another sandbox.

## Open: wave heights blow up at the North Pole

In the smoke run, significant wave height reaches 88 m at the node nearest the pole (89.90°N) after
2 days and spreads south to about 78°N, under ordinary winds of about 12 m/s. It is not the currents
(about 0.1 m/s there) and not a mesh defect (every node north of 88.5°N has 6 neighbours).

WW3 computes triangle geometry in plain longitude–latitude. It fixes triangles that cross the 180°
meridian, and its code comments name the case of a triangle that contains the pole, but leaves that
triangle as it is (`FIX_PERIODCITY` in `w3triamd.F90`). Our pole triangle spans 258° of longitude;
`wu025r004`'s spans 196°. In a 24-day run with ERA5 winds (3–6 m/s near the pole), `wu025r004` stays at
about 4 m at most there. A run of `wu025r005` with the same winds is the like-for-like test. A likely fix
is a small hole in the mesh at the pole, for example north of 88.5°N.

Ice does not hide this today: without CICE, CESM's WW3 cap turns all ice effects off, so waves grow
under the Arctic ice. Choosing the ice physics is a separate open question (see [WW3 manuals](ww3_manuals.md)).

## Comparison with the NOAA mesh

A 2-day rerun of an earlier `wu025r004` run forced by ERA5 winds reproduces it to within 4 mm of wave
height, so that 24-day run is the reference. The matching `wu025r005` run (same winds, same settings,
hourly point output at 638 locations, including NDBC buoys) is next; observations come after.
